title: fix(spec): the pure-annotation build plugin marks real calls only, so the published text equals its source (#20686)
body:
Fixes #20686
Clause-②: no

The `pure-schema-construction` build plugin (`packages/spec/tsup.config.ts`) now marks real calls of `lazySchema` / `strictObject` / `defineForm` only, and never touches text. The published `@objectstack/spec/migrations` bundle carries the source's text again. The one affected D3 entry, `18.dashboard-widget-stage-order-non-funnel-refused`, has no text change.

## What changed

- **`annotatePureCalls(source, fileName)`** replaces the line-prefix rule. The TypeScript parser drives the scanner. Every `CallExpression` whose callee is one of the three names gets the PURE annotation at the start of the call, whether the callee is bare (`lazySchema(…)`) or a property-access member (`z.strictObject(…)`). String and template text, comments, JSDoc and declarations are not call expressions, so they are never touched. A call inside a template substitution is code, and it is marked (that behaviour is decided here and pinned). The output is the source plus inserted annotations, and nothing else.
- The esbuild `Plugin` type is now read off tsup's `Options['esbuildPlugins']`. This package has no direct `esbuild` dependency, so a bare `'esbuild'` type import resolves for no type checker. `ts.resolveModuleName` from this file answers UNRESOLVED. The new test puts this file in front of `tsconfig.scripts.json`.
- `pureSchemaConstruction` and `mainConfig` are named exports, for the test. tsup reads only the default export.
- New test `packages/spec/scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts`, in the `local` project (6 cases). It adds no gate.
- `.changeset/20686-pure-plugin-skips-strings.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch.

## Why a parse and not a bare `ts.createScanner` pass

Whether `/` starts a regex literal and whether `}` resumes a template are grammar questions. The scanner answers them only when the parser asks it to rescan. Measured over `packages/spec/src` at 3693a1b50d (1774 files, test files excluded): a `createScanner` loop without those rescans reports 1538 calls where the syntax tree has 1727. It loses 191 real calls, because every regex literal that contains a quote is mis-lexed. It also marks 2 mentions inside comments: one in the `defineForm` JSDoc `@example` (`ui/view.zod.ts:7013`) and one in a line comment (`:7042`). So the positions are read off the syntax tree that the parser builds with that same scanner. Parse cost: the new rule parses the 249 files that name a marked constructor (the old rule rewrote 212). The census that ran both rules over all of `src` took 1.2 s.

## Annotation census

**Source level** (insertion positions over `packages/spec/src` non-test files, old rule vs new):

| | old rule | new |
|---|---|---|
| insertions | 1730 | 1727 |

The old rule's extra or misplaced insertions, all in non-call positions:

- `migrations/registry.ts:8608`: **inside a string** (the `acceptanceCriteria` of `dashboard-widget-stage-order-non-funnel-refused`). This one shipped.
- `migrations/entries/semantic/18.dashboard-widget-stage-order-non-funnel-refused.ts:59`: the same string in the entry source. No bundle imports the entry file. Only the generated registry copy is bundled.
- `ui/view.zod.ts:7032`: `export function defineForm(`, a **declaration**. esbuild drops a comment there, so it has no effect on the bundles.
- `data/driver/turso.zod.ts:469`: `z.strictObject({`. The annotation **moved** from after the `z.` to the start of the call. See the note below.

No new position exists beyond that move. Real calls with a type argument or a space before the paren: 0 in `src`. So including them changes nothing today.

**Bundle level** (tsup JS pass, all 48 `.js` / `.mjs` bundles, base plugin vs fixed plugin, same source tree):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| PURE annotations, all bundles | 17202 | 17220 (+18) |
| `migrations/index.js` / `.mjs` | 82 / 82 | 81 / 81 (the in-string one removed) |
| the 20 bundles that reach the Turso schema (10 entries, ESM and CJS) | n | n + 1 each (the moved member-call annotation) |
| the marker inside `` z.strictObject(DashboardWidgetSchema.shape) `` | 2 | 0 |
| bundles differing once every annotation is stripped | | 0 of 48 |

So the published code is byte-identical apart from annotations: −2 in the string and +20 at the one member call.

**The member-call annotation (bounded in-place fix).** esbuild 0.28.1 (the version tsup resolves) drops an annotation written after a member access's dot. Measured on an input carrying both spellings: an unused `const` initialised from `z.` + PURE + `strictObject({…})` is kept, and its PURE annotation is gone from the output. An unused `const` initialised from PURE + `z.strictObject({…})` is dropped. So the old rule's output at `turso.zod.ts:469` marked nothing. The new rule puts the annotation where esbuild honours it, because it marks call expressions. It is the same defect class (the plugin wrote an annotation at a token that is not a call start). The fix is mechanical, pinned by the fixture test, in the file this claim holds, and adds no verification surface.

## Tree-shake control

Measured with a consumer bundle per row: esbuild, `bundle`, `minify`, `treeShaking`, `zod` external. Sizes are bytes against the before tree, the after tree, and the before tree with every annotation stripped (what the plugin buys):

| consumer imports | before | after | no annotations |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FieldSchema` from `./data` | 231,683 | 231,683 | 551,411 |
| `TursoConfigSchema` from `./data` | 173,044 | 173,044 | 551,411 |
| `defineStack` from the root | 954,689 | 954,689 | 968,107 |
| `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR` from `./migrations` | 1,548,424 | 1,548,408 | 1,548,521 |

Tree-shaking is unchanged. The −16 bytes on `./migrations` is the 16-character marker that left the string.

## The test, and how it reads the build

No spec test reads the real `packages/spec/dist`. Only gates do, and they run after the build step in `lint.yml`. turbo's `@objectstack/spec#test` depends on `^build` only, and spec has no workspace dependency. So in CI, `dist` is either absent or built in parallel when the suite runs. A test that read it would be skipped or racy there. This test therefore runs the real build itself. It calls tsup's own `build()` with the exported `mainConfig` (the plugin, target and treeshake included) over `src/migrations/index.ts`. It writes into a temp directory under the package's `node_modules/.cache` (so the bundle's `zod` import resolves), imports the bundle and compares:

- `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR`, `MIGRATION_MAJORS`, `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR`, `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` and `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` must equal the source values exactly. Markers are **not** stripped before comparing: stripped, the buggy build compares equal too. A control requires at least one annotation in that bundle, so the equality cannot hold vacuously for a build that ran no plugin.
- A fixture quotes every marked name in a single-quoted and a double-quoted string, template text, a template substitution, a regex literal, JSDoc, and trailing block and line comments, next to a declaration and the three real call shapes. It is built through the same `build()`. Each string survives byte-identical, and the real calls carry the annotation at the call start.
- Four `annotatePureCalls` cases pin positions directly. They cover the unparsed hand-back, untouched non-calls, every call shape, and that removing the insertions gives the source back.

## Ablation

The fix was committed first (`7189a7c485`). `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the plugin's call to `annotatePureCalls` with the old line-prefix rule. The anchor went from x1 to x0, and the blob from `7adc1d65404d` to `e73d50e2a72e`. The run, under the verify lock:

- **2 failed | 4 passed.** The built `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR` differs from the source at entry `dashboard-widget-stage-order-non-funnel-refused`, field `acceptanceCriteria`: the live entry.
- The fixture build fails with esbuild `Unexpected "export"`. The old rule wrote an annotation inside a trailing block comment and closed it early. That is the comment-in-comment hazard the old docblock cites.
- The four `annotatePureCalls` cases stay green, as expected: they call the function, not the plugin.

The restore was proven by the tool: blob after restore = blob at HEAD = `7adc1d65404d`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty. No `dist` is involved. The test imports the plugin from source and builds in-test, so there was no rebuild leg.

## Verification (at `7272847e14`: the branch merged with `origin/main` `5f6b63a6fd`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`: green. `dist` has 0 in-string markers and 17220 annotations.
- `vitest run scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts`: 6 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: 585 files passed, 17211 tests passed, 1 todo.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: green. `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json --listFiles` includes the new test and `tsup.config.ts`.
- `dispatch-gates --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 67 derived. `--ran`: 65 run, all exit 0, and **2 NOT MEASURED** (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET):
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs the `dist` of every workspace package (86 named). Spec's own half was measured directly: all 24 `require` export conditions of `@objectstack/spec` load.
  - `check:type-check-debt` needs 30 workspace dependencies built. `@objectstack/spec` is graduated from that ledger, and its own `typecheck` is green above.
  - Both are declared narrowings, and CI runs them.
- `check:lean-entry-closure` ran against an objectql closure rebuilt at this head. `check:query-options-erasure` ran in 307 s.
- After this head, `origin/main` moved 4 commits (to `7fa67dada3`). None touches `packages/spec`. The derivation files that changed (`scripts/pm/ensure-pm-labels.sh` and two `scripts/pm/fleet-write/` modules) are unrelated to these paths.

## Acceptance notes

- The card attributes the altered text to the entry's `reason` (printed as `why:`). It is the entry's `acceptanceCriteria`, which `os migrate meta` prints as the `verify:` line (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts:380`). The premise holds. Only the field name differs.
- The old rule also rewrote 56 positions in `src/**/*.test.ts` files. No entry's graph reaches a test file, so none of them shipped.
